styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Al-Balad's coral houses, old souqs and the city's galleries.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Red Sea fish, Hijazi street food and long evening meals.

styles.label: Beach
styles.blurb: Corniche swims, Obhur boat rides and Red Sea sunsets.

stays.why: Step out into the old town's alleys and souqs. Best for history and photography; some streets are quiet at night.
Waterfront hotels with sea views and easy walks at sunset. Good for first-time visitors.
Central and calm, close to the Corniche and good restaurants. A practical base for most trips.
North-coast resorts and marina boats. Quieter and beach-focused; far from Al-Balad.

food: Eat Hijazi food: sayadiyah (fish and rice), saleeg (rice porridge) and mutabbaq stuffed pastries.
Fish is the local star. Try a Red Sea fish grill; prices vary by catch, so ask per kilo first.
Al-Balad evenings: small cafeterias and juice stalls, about SR 10–30 for a snack.
Book ahead for popular seafood and Lebanese restaurants on the Corniche, especially on weekends.
Alcohol is not sold in Jeddah. Expect tea, coffee and fresh juices instead.
more_time: Add a day for the Red Sea: a boat trip from Obhur marina (about SR 200 for an hour) or a dive check with local operators.
History fans can take the high-speed train to Medina for a night; book seats early.
Swap one city day for a desert or wadi trip outside Jeddah; check on the day for operator schedules and heat.

recommend.why: Two nights covers Al-Balad, the Corniche and a Red Sea evening; add a night for a boat trip or a day outside the city.

month_notes: Jan: mild days around 27°C, cool nights near 20°C. A few rain days; bring a light layer.
Feb: similar to January, about 28°C by day. Comfortable for walking Al-Balad.
Mar: warming to 30°C, almost no rain. Good beach weather begins.
Apr: hot at 32°C and humid. Sightsee early morning and after sunset.
May: 34°C and rising humidity. Plan indoor breaks in the middle of the day.
Jun: hot and humid, 35°C. Drink water often; the sea breeze helps on the Corniche.
Jul: the hottest month, 36°C with muggy nights near 28°C. Go out at sunrise or after dark.
Aug: as hot as July, 36°C. Keep outdoor time short and stay near water or AC.
Sep: still hot at 35°C. Evenings slowly improve late in the month.
Oct: cooling to 34°C with a little rain possible. Better for long walks.
Nov: pleasant at 31°C with a few rain days. A good month for the old town.
Dec: mild at 29°C, cool nights near 22°C. The most rain days of the year; pack a light rain jacket.

climate_guide.summary: Hot desert coast: sunny most of the year, humid summers and a short, mild winter with a little rain.

items.title: Best time: November to March
items.text: Days around 27–31°C and nights near 20–24°C. Ideal for Al-Balad, the Corniche and boats.

items.title: Summer is hot and humid (June to September)
items.text: Highs of 35–36°C and muggy nights near 28–29°C. Sightsee early or late; rest indoors at midday.

items.title: Humid by the sea
items.text: Sticky evenings from May to October. Light, loose clothing helps more than heavy cotton.

items.title: Little rain, mostly in winter
items.text: Rain days peak in December (about 4) and November (about 3). Showers are usually short.

items.title: Strong sun all year
items.text: Even in winter, use sunscreen, a hat and sunglasses. Shade is scarce on the Corniche.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light breathable clothes, a hat and sunscreen; a light layer for cool winter nights and strong AC; modest clothing for mosques and the old town.

transit.best: Ride apps or taxis for most trips; walk in Al-Balad and take a taxi along the Corniche.

modes.text: No metro yet. Don't plan around rail inside the city.
City buses are common and timetabled on Google Maps. Cheap but slow; SAPTCO covers long-distance routes.
Green taxis and ride apps are plentiful; Uber and Careem both work. Agree the fare before you set off, especially from the airport.
Easy to rent and fuel is among the cheapest in the world. Watch for speed cameras and heavy traffic.
Best in Al-Balad. The Corniche is long, so plan on a taxi for the full stretch.
A high-speed rail line links Jeddah with Mecca and Medina. Book seats early.
Boats from Obhur marina are for views, not transport; about SR 200 for an hour.
